subject.title: fix(autoreview): allow safe Python runtime references

question: Is the final accepted Python expression grammar narrow enough to permit these runtime references without weakening autoreview's credential-disclosure boundary?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes a security allow boundary, and tests cannot fully determine the repository's acceptable disclosure policy or tolerance for future parser edge cases.

options.title: Approve after boundary review
options.body: Review every accepted AST and token shape, require inspectable downstream proof, and merge if the classifier remains fail closed outside those shapes.

options.title: Narrow the accepted grammar
options.body: Replace the broad classifier with a smaller set of expression forms limited to the concrete downstream failure before reconsidering merge.

options.title: Retain current strict scanning
options.body: Decline the exemption if avoiding any additional credential-disclosure surface outweighs the reported false-positive cost.

recommendation.title: Approve after boundary review
recommendation.body: Review every accepted AST and token shape, require inspectable downstream proof, and merge if the classifier remains fail closed outside those shapes.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main history most strongly connects steipete to the autoreview scanner's design and prior maintenance.
